title: Not Every Cue Is Evidence: Cue Supportability for Forensic Distillation in Face Forgery Detection
review_scope: Official arXiv HTML abstract, method §§3.1–3.4, main tables, human study, Appendix C evaluator protocol, limitations, and references [1]–[67].
construct: Correct-answer/wrong-evidence; cue factual correctness, visual verifiability, spatial specificity; transfer utility and visual sensitivity.
empirical_evidence: Eight face-forgery benchmarks; 3,600 image-cue pairs each rated by three of ten annotators; 1,000 FF++ cue human-support correlation; evaluator vs human-majority κ=.72 and 87.4% accuracy.
boundary: Preprint; face-forgery and single-turn English only. Human ratings validate cue support and judge calibration, not user reliance. Intervention is attribution-guided high-vs-low token zeroing, not complete causal necessity/sufficiency.
